hook: I want to **avoid a family fight** after I'm gone.
hook_q: How do I make a valid will?

slides.title: Who can **make** a will?
slides.body: Anyone of sound mind who is not a minor. Being deaf, dumb or blind is no bar if you know what you're doing. Not knowing, due to illness, intoxication or any other cause, is.

timeline.text: You **sign** or put your mark, or someone signs in your presence and at your direction.
At least **two witnesses** see you sign, or get your personal acknowledgment of it.
Each witness **signs** in your presence, not necessarily together.

slides.title: **No legal jargon** needed.
slides.body: A will doesn't need technical words or legal terms, as long as your intentions can be understood. No particular form of attestation is needed either.

slides.title: Registration is **optional.**
slides.body: The Registration Act lists wills among documents that may be registered, so it's your choice. A will can be presented for registration, or deposited, at any time.

slides.title: Made under pressure? **Void.**
slides.body: A will, or any part of it, made because of fraud, coercion, or pressure that takes away your free agency, is void.

slides.title: You can **change your mind.**
slides.body: You can revoke or change a will at any time while you're still competent to make one: by a new will or codicil, a writing executed like a will, or by destroying it to revoke it.

slides.title: Muslim? **Different rules.**
slides.body: These Indian Succession Act rules on wills do not apply to wills of Muslims. For Hindus, Buddhists, Sikhs and Jains, the rules above apply, but marriage does not revoke their will.
slides.ref: Indian Succession Act 1925 · Sec 57, 58(1), Schedule III · Uttarakhand UCC 2024
slides.note: Uttarakhand: State's Uniform Civil Code applies

sources: Indian Succession Act, 1925 – Sections 2(h), 57, 58, 59, 61, 62, 63, 70, 74 and Schedule III
Uniform Civil Code, Uttarakhand, 2024 (in force 27 Jan 2025, PIB)
caption:
Want your wishes followed after you're gone? Here's how a valid will is made. 👇

1️⃣ Anyone of sound mind who is not a minor can make a will
2️⃣ Sign it (or put your mark), and have at least two witnesses sign in your presence
3️⃣ No legal jargon is needed, and no particular form of attestation
4️⃣ Registering a will is optional, and can be done at any time
5️⃣ A will made through fraud or coercion is void
6️⃣ You can revoke or change it at any time
⚠️ These rules don't apply to wills of Muslims. In Uttarakhand, the State's Uniform Civil Code, 2024 now governs wills of residents (except Scheduled Tribes)

Source: Indian Succession Act, 1925 (Sec 57, 58, 59, 61, 62, 63, 70, 74); Registration Act, 1908 (Sec 18, 27)
